title: The Moth Hollow Tapes
subtitle: Reopened January 2026 — Assigned to you, Detective

stages.detectiveNote: The files are incomplete. Some evidence appears damaged or intentionally removed. Start with the station records and Naomi Vale's original disappearance report.
stages.dispatchMessage: Detective [NAME] — review the initial evidence package and determine the date Naomi Vale disappeared.
stages.unlockQuestion: What was the official date Naomi Vale disappeared?
hints: The answer appears in the official report, not the station records.
Check the Missing Person Report carefully. The date appears near the top of the page.

stages.detectiveNote: Evelyn says Naomi left around 10, but the emergency call wasn't placed until nearly midnight. Someone's timeline doesn't add up. And that humming in the background of the caller recording — I've heard that before somewhere.
stages.dispatchMessage: Detective [NAME] — the witness timeline doesn't match the emergency response. What time was the 911 call placed?
stages.unlockQuestion: What time was the 911 call placed?
hints: Compare the witness statement against the emergency records.
The exact time appears in the 911 transcript, at the top of the document.
The emergency call was placed at 11:42 PM.

stages.detectiveNote: The phone records show the same number calling in every week during Naomi's shift. And that memo footer — there's a URL in there. Barely visible but it's there. I need to look at that.

Lena was ahead of everyone. She wasn't just researching Naomi — she was building a case. And then she vanished too. Whatever she found, someone didn't want it found. That note on the back of her photo — check the static. What does that mean?
stages.dispatchMessage: Detective [NAME] — Lena believed the broadcasts were intentionally designed to influence listeners. What term did she use to describe the technique?
stages.unlockQuestion: What term did Lena use to describe the broadcast technique?
hints: Lena uses the term multiple times throughout her archived blog posts.
It's a psychological term — she uses it to describe how repeated audio was changing listeners' behavior.

stages.detectiveNote: Maybe the recordings weren't dangerous because of what they contained. Maybe they were dangerous because people believed they were. Voss is a psychologist. He would know exactly how to make that work. And the phrases in these clinical notes — I've read those exact words somewhere else in this case.
stages.dispatchMessage: Detective [NAME] — Naomi believed someone inside the station was manipulating the broadcasts. Who had unauthorized archive access?
stages.unlockQuestion: Who had unauthorized archive access to the station?
hints: The internal complaint memo narrows archive access to a specific individual.
Cross-reference who had consulting access to the station from the staff directory.
Dr. Elias Voss had direct archive access.

stages.detectiveNote: The tower. Everything keeps coming back to the tower. And Voss keeps saying memory is easy to shape — like he's not even hiding it anymore. Like he knows no one will ever prove it. There's a code on that evidence bag in the search photos. I need to look more carefully.
stages.dispatchMessage: Detective [NAME] — where did Naomi confront Voss the night she disappeared?
stages.unlockQuestion: Where did Naomi confront Voss the night she disappeared?
hints: The answer appears after unlocking the hidden incident materials. Think about the search photos.
Look at what appears in the background of the forest search photographs.
Naomi confronted Voss at the relay tower outside town.

stages.detectiveNote: It's all here. Every piece connects. The broadcasts, the conditioning, the cover-up, the tower. Voss designed all of it. And he's still out there.
stages.dispatchMessage: Detective [NAME] — you have enough to reconstruct what happened. Submit your final case assessment.

finalQuestions.prompt: Based on the full evidence, what best describes Dr. Voss's role in the Moth Hollow broadcasts?
options: He was an innocent bystander who noticed the broadcasts
He designed and embedded the broadcasts as part of a psychological experiment
He was a victim of the experiment like everyone else
He was attempting to expose the experiments from inside the station

finalQuestions.prompt: Select the true purpose of the recordings.
Why was the evidence surrounding Naomi's disappearance contradictory and incomplete?
acceptedAnswers: so no one would find out

solution.caseClosedText: Dr. Elias Voss conducted an unauthorized psychological experiment using WHLW 88.3 broadcasts between 1994 and 1998. Naomi Vale discovered the truth through a recovered recording in the station archive. She confronted Voss at the relay tower on October 14, 1998. She did not survive that confrontation. Voss concealed her death and systematically fragmented the evidence. Years later, Lena Hart independently uncovered the manipulation — and then she too disappeared. The case is closed. But not every question has been answered.

caseBriefing.body:
In 2025, a private archivist recovered a collection of sealed investigative files from a decommissioned storage facility in rural West Virginia.

The files had been classified under a departmental case closure order issued in October 1998. The closure was signed before a formal investigation was completed.

The archivist has since gone quiet. The files remain.

The case assigned to you was never officially solved.

Naomi Vale, 26, overnight radio host at WHLW 88.3 in Moth Hollow, West Virginia — disappeared October 14, 1998. Her vehicle was found two miles from the station. No body was recovered. The investigation was suspended eleven days later.

The evidence in this archive is incomplete. Some files appear damaged. Others appear to have been intentionally removed.

What remains is what you have. Work with it.

— SEALED FILE CO. ARCHIVE DIVISION
caseBriefing.dismissText: I HAVE READ AND UNDERSTOOD — BEGIN INVESTIGATION

stage-1.body:
Three additional files have been located in the archive.

The original detective's notes indicate these were part of the initial evidence package but were catalogued separately from the primary case briefing. The reason for the separation is not noted.

Review all materials before proceeding.

stage-3.body:
The archivist who originally recovered these files included supplementary materials gathered during research into the Moth Hollow case.

These materials are not part of the original 1998 evidence package. They were collected between 2002 and 2007 by a secondary researcher who independently investigated the case.

That researcher's name was Lena Hart.

stage-5.body:
The original search of the area surrounding the WHLW relay tower was conducted over three days in October 1998. Initial search results were logged but not included in the primary case file.

The following materials were recovered from a secondary storage box associated with this case. They appear to have been separated from the main file at some point between 1998 and 2003.

revealCharacters.name: Dr. Elias Voss
revealCharacters.verdict: Conducted an unauthorized psychological experiment using WHLW 88.3 broadcasts between 1994 and 1998. He designed the experiment, chose the subjects, manufactured the evidence of manipulation. When Naomi discovered the truth, he ensured her silence. He has never been charged. As of 2026, he remains in Moth Hollow.

revealCharacters.name: Naomi Elise Vale
revealCharacters.verdict: Discovered the truth through a recording recovered from the station archive. Confronted Voss at the relay tower on October 14, 1998. Did not survive that confrontation. Her death was made to look like a disappearance. She was 26 years old.

revealCharacters.name: Lena Hart
revealCharacters.verdict: Independently uncovered fragments of the experiment years after Naomi's disappearance. Vanished in 2007 before she could make her findings public. Her research blog was taken offline. Her current whereabouts are unknown.

revealCharacters.name: Evelyn Pike
revealCharacters.verdict: Altered broadcast logs and lied in her witness statement — not to protect Voss, but to protect Naomi's reputation. She feared the unusual broadcasts would be blamed on Naomi after her disappearance. She had no knowledge of the experiment. She acted out of loyalty.

revealCharacters.name: Sheriff Dale Mercer
revealCharacters.verdict: Closed the original case prematurely to protect his department from scrutiny over early investigation failures. Did not know about the experiment. Did not know Voss caused Naomi's death. His failures allowed Voss to avoid accountability permanently.

revealCharacters.name: Gabriel Hart
revealCharacters.verdict: Has been quietly investigating since Lena's disappearance in 2007. He is still looking. He does not know the case has been formally reopened.

naomi-vale.footerRef: FILE: PERS-001 / CASE: WHL-1998-001 / STATUS: OPEN
naomi-vale.summary: Naomi Vale hosted the overnight shift at WHLW 88.3 for approximately one year before her disappearance. Colleagues described her as warm and professional. No body was recovered. Her vehicle was found abandoned on Tower Road two days after she was reported missing. The case was suspended after eleven days with no primary suspect named.

statement.quote: "Somebody is changing things after hours. I've found tapes I didn't put there. Recordings have been altered. I believe I know who is responsible."

dr-voss.footerRef: FILE: PERS-002 / CASE: WHL-1998-001 / STATUS: ACTIVE REVIEW
dr-voss.summary: Dr. Elias Voss served as a consulting psychologist for WHLW's Community Outreach Program beginning in 1993. His role is described vaguely in station records. He had authorized access to the station during business hours. His connection to Naomi Vale's case emerged through the station's internal files.

statement.quote:
"Memory is incredibly easy to shape, Detective. People often believe they remember things that never occurred. And sometimes they can't remember what did."

"Is that a yes or a no?"

"It's an observation."

evelyn-pike.summary: Evelyn Pike was the primary technician on duty during Naomi Vale's overnight shifts. She was among the last confirmed station staff to see Naomi before her disappearance. Her witness statement and the official emergency record do not align.

statement.quote: "Naomi seemed stressed. The phones kept ringing after hours — more than usual. She left earlier than scheduled. Around 10, maybe just before. I stayed late to lock up."

sheriff-mercer.footerRef: FILE: PERS-004 / CASE: WHL-1998-001 / STATUS: UNDER REVIEW
sheriff-mercer.summary: Sheriff Dale Mercer led the original investigation into Naomi Vale's disappearance in October 1998. The investigation was closed after eleven days with no charges filed and no primary suspect named. A review of the case files has identified several procedural gaps that were never formally addressed.

statement.quote: "Investigation has produced no physical evidence sufficient to establish criminal cause of disappearance. Case is suspended pending new information. The department extends its condolences to the Vale family."

lena-hart.summary: Lena Hart independently investigated Naomi Vale's disappearance as a journalism research project beginning in 2006. She disappeared in March 2007 before completing or publishing her findings. A collection of her archived research materials has recently resurfaced and is now part of this case file.

statement.quote: "The conditioning patterns in the WHLW broadcast record are not accidental. Someone designed this. I don't know who. But I know why Naomi disappeared."
